ideas.description: Base: E060 code, which is the E057 tip (static shapes, max(dim).values pool, Muon floor 0.05) plus E060's vectorized dirac init and fused fp16 normalization in prepare. Both prepare changes are math-neutral, so the result still belongs to the pooled family, which E060 brings to 8 runs with a mean of 0.7531. Change only the head's Muon learning rate: set it to 0.5x the filter Muon LR (0.12 peak, same schedule shape and floor) as its own 0-d GPU tensor, so nothing recompiles. Leave everything else unchanged. Score it twice. Instrumentation only: log the submission source hash and a per-seed checksum of the final weights and BN buffers (for H4.4.1).
ideas.expected: Time 4.66-4.69 s, the same as E060 within 0.5% (4.675 s), so about -0.9% against the 4.717 s tip whenever a run is feasible. Two-run pooled accuracy 0.7535-0.7550. A pool of 0.7540 or higher, i.e. +0.09 pp over the family's 0.7531 and a 3-run pool of at least 0.7545 together with E049, passes the H4 rule and makes this the new tip at about 4.67 s. If both runs land at 0.7530 or below, head LR is closed (E049 was noise).

ideas.description: Base: E060 code. After 20% of total steps, which falls inside the 16 px phase, set the whitening-stem bias to requires_grad=False. The stem's weights are already frozen, so the stem then has no trainable parameters, and autograd skips group-1 conv1's input gradient (dgrad) for every later step at 16, 24 and 32 px. Compile separate static train graphs keyed by whether the bias takes a gradient, and warm up every (resolution, flag) shape in build on synthetic data. Remove the bias from the SGD foreach step at the switch, or give it a zero LR with a None grad that is skipped. Change nothing else. Before scoring, check in an untimed run that the compiled backward graph has no stem-side convolution_backward input-grad. Score it twice.
ideas.expected: Time 4.60-4.65 s, i.e. -0.5 to -1.5% against E060's 4.675 s and -1.5 to -2.5% against the 4.717 s tip. Most of the gain should come from the energy-bound 32 px tail. Two-run pooled accuracy 0.7522-0.7545, within noise of 0.7531. If the drop against E060 is under 0.3%, the dgrad is not being skipped, or it is negligible, and the FLOP channel of H2.15 is refuted. If accuracy pools at 0.7540 or higher, it also supports H8.1's bias-LR channel.

ideas.description: Base: E060 code. Change only the schedule to E047's 2@16 + 1.5@24 + 4@32 px: 7.5 total epochs with step-indexed resolution switches, and LR warmup/decay, the Muon floor, EMA, lookahead and the renorm cadence all rescaled to the new total step count, as E047 did. All three bs-1536 static shapes are already warmed up in build. Score it twice. This is the equal-time reshuffle against the 3@16 + 1@24 swap that the current tip uses.
ideas.expected: Time 4.66-4.71 s: E047 matched E046 within 0.2%, so this should be equal to E060 within 0.5%. Two-run pooled accuracy 0.7535-0.7555, i.e. +0.05 to +0.2 pp over 0.7531. A pool of 0.7540 or higher makes it the new tip at about 4.68 s (H4 rule) and leaves room for a later fractional trim. If both runs land at 0.7530 or below, E047's 0.7558 was a lucky draw and the 3@16 swap is as good as the reshuffle.

ideas.description: Base: E060 code. The change is Inductor kernel tuning only, aimed at the fused BN/GELU/elementwise Triton kernels, which take about 30% of GPU time (E052). Set torch._inductor.config.coordinate_descent_tuning=True and torch._inductor.config.max_autotune_pointwise=True (the net already compiles with max-autotune) before compiling the net, then recompile and warm up every static train shape plus the eval path in build. Log build time; it must stay under 600 s, and if tuning would exceed that, drop max_autotune_pointwise first. The math is unchanged apart from reduction order. Smoke-test that the loss stays finite for 10 steps before scoring.
ideas.expected: Time -0.5 to -2% against E060's 4.675 s (about 4.58-4.65 s), with the largest saving in the 24 and 32 px phases, whose elementwise kernels are energy- and memory-bound. Accuracy within noise (0.7520-0.7545). A drop under 0.3% means Inductor's default configs for these kernels are already near-optimal, so the next step is a hand-written fused BN-apply+GELU kernel, and only if H2.16.1 shows at least 4 passes.

ideas.description: Observational. Run an untimed side script on the E060 code with the same build and one trial on seed 0. Use torch.profiler for about 20 steps of the 32 px phase at bs 1536, and also for 20 steps at 24 px. Per conv layer, record the forward and backward kernel list, the time share of Triton elementwise/reduction kernels against cuDNN conv kernels, and the bytes read and written per BN/GELU kernel relative to the fp16 activation size, i.e. the number of passes over the activation. In the same profile, record per-layer conv time for group 2 (input for H2.13.2). For the scored row, rerun the E060 code unchanged as an extra family variance sample. Log the per-seed weight checksums (H4.4.1) and the cuDNN kernel names per layer and shape (H4.5.1).
ideas.expected: Scored row: about 4.675 s, accuracy 0.752-0.755, which adds one run to the family pool. The profile should show elementwise/reduction kernels at 25-35% of 32 px GPU time and at least 4 activation-sized passes per BN+GELU (forward stats, apply+GELU, backward recompute, backward reduction+apply). If they take under 15% of the time or already run at 2 passes or fewer, H2.16 is refuted and the fused-kernel line is closed.

ideas.description: Base: E060 code. Apply Fable's tail at equal total steps. The Muon and SGD LR decay reaches its floor (0.05x for Muon, unchanged for SGD) about 4% of steps early and holds there until the end. Over the last ~8 steps, update a light final EMA every 4 steps (ema = 0.7*ema + 0.3*net with torch._foreach_lerp_, buffers allocated in build and reset in prepare). It replaces the end of the lookahead-EMA ramp, and evaluation uses those EMA weights, with BN buffers copied from the net. Change nothing else, and score it twice.
ideas.expected: Time within 0.5% of E060 (4.65-4.70 s). Two-run pooled accuracy 0.7525-0.7550. A pool of 0.7540 or higher (H4 rule) makes it a zero-cost margin source and the new tip. If it lands within ±0.1 pp of 0.7531, it closes end-of-schedule tuning for Muon along with E057.

ideas.description: Base: E060 code. Change only the peak Muon LR of the conv filters from 0.24 to 0.28, through the existing 0-d tensor so nothing recompiles. The head keeps its own LR multiplier exactly as on the base, so the head's absolute LR also rises with the filter LR. With bs 1536 and only about 256 steps, the bs-1024 LR optimum (flat at 0.20-0.24, E034) may have shifted upward. Score it twice.
ideas.expected: Time unchanged (±0.5%, about 4.675 s). Two-run pooled accuracy 0.7520-0.7550. A pool of 0.7545 or higher supports H7.1.3 and becomes a margin source. A pool within ±0.15 pp of 0.7531 means the lr optimum transfers and Muon lr is closed on the bs-1536 tip. A pool of 0.7515 or lower means 0.24 is already at or above the optimum.

drop.reason: Superseded by the H2.15.1 idea, which runs on the current E060/E057 base instead of the stale E046 tip. It also freezes the bias with requires_grad=False, so it removes group-1 conv1's dgrad (a FLOP lever) as well as testing the H8.1 bias channel. I068 only zeroes the LR, which skips no compute.

structured_output.summary:
The current state: the E057 tip runs at 4.717 s, and its same-math family now pools to about 0.7531 over 8 runs, right at the 0.753 gate. E060's prepare speedup (-0.9%) is math-neutral and bankable, so every new idea builds on the E060 code. Banking any speedup needs about +0.1-0.2 pp of accuracy at no extra time, or math-neutral time cuts that keep accuracy in the noise band. The queue is 7 ideas: 4 exploit and 3 explore.

Exploit:
- Head Muon LR at 0.5x, scored twice (H7.3.2). The best single zero-cost signal so far is E049.
- Freezing the whitening bias with requires_grad=False after 20% of steps (H2.15.1). This is a FLOP lever that drops group-1 conv1's input gradient, and it doubles as a test of H8.1. It replaces the queued I068, which ran on the stale E046 base and saved no compute.
- E047's equal-time 2@16 + 1.5@24 + 4@32 reshuffle on the current base (H2.10.3).
- Inductor coordinate-descent and pointwise autotuning aimed at the BN/GELU elementwise kernels, which take about 30% of GPU time (H2.16.2).

Explore:
- A profile of passes over each activation and per-layer cost (H2.16.1, also feeding H2.13.2). Its scored row is an extra variance sample, with weight checksums and cuDNN kernel names logged for H4.4.1 and H4.5.1.
- Fable's floor-held tail plus a light final EMA (H6.5.2).
- Muon filter LR 0.28 on the bs-1536 regime (H7.1.3).

Every accuracy lever is scored twice and judged against the pooled 0.7531 mean, following the H4 promotion rule.
